manifest.title: Elephant: Touch to wave
manifest.footnote: Use a micro:bit V2 and a 360-degree positional servo on Nezha S2. The simulator can show events and LEDs; confirm movement on the physical build. Adjust the linkage to its working range.

reference.source: User-supplied image: on logo touched; repeat 10; 360 servo 2 angle 180; pause 500 ms; angle 0.
changes: Add a second 500 ms pause after angle 0 so the servo has time to return before the next command.
Introduce Running and an if guard to ignore touches during a wave sequence.
Show a diamond while running and a tick after the sequence finishes.

stages.title: Touch to move the servo
stages.concept: A touch event starts a servo command.
stages.adds: Add on logo touched. Inside it, set the 360-degree servo on S2 to 180 degrees.
stages.predict: What happens when you touch the logo?
observe: Touch the logo on micro:bit V2.
Physical build: S2 moves toward 180 degrees.
Touch again: the same target is sent.
stages.question: Which block starts the movement?

stages.title: Move out and return
stages.concept: Commands run in order; a pause gives movement time.
stages.adds: Keep angle 180. Add pause 500 ms, then set the same S2 servo to angle 0.
stages.predict: Which angle is sent after the pause?
observe: Physical build: watch one outward-and-return motion.
stages.question: Why is the pause between the angles?

stages.title: Give the return time
stages.concept: The return movement also needs a pause.
stages.adds: Add another pause 500 ms after angle 0. Keep both pauses for the next step.
stages.predict: Where should the second pause go?
observe: One cycle now has 1000 ms of pauses.
stages.question: What could happen without return time?

stages.title: Repeat ten waves
stages.concept: A repeat loop runs a whole movement cycle.
stages.adds: Put both servo commands and both pauses inside repeat 10. Touch once; wait for it to finish.
stages.predict: How many outward movements will run?
observe: Wait until all ten finish before touching again.
stages.question: Which four blocks must repeat together?

stages.title: Remember when it is running
stages.concept: A Boolean variable stores the busy state.
stages.adds: Create Running (false by default). Show a tick on start. Set true before waving and false after the final tick.
stages.predict: When should Running change to false?
stages.question: Does storing Running block extra touches yet?
stages.code:
let Running = false
basic.showIcon(IconNames.Yes)
input.onLogoEvent(TouchButtonEvent.Touched, function () {
    Running = true
    basic.showIcon(IconNames.SmallDiamond)
    for (let index = 0; index < 10; index++) {
        neZha.setServoAngel(neZha.ServoTypeList._360, neZha.ServoList.S2, 180)
        basic.pause(500)
        neZha.setServoAngel(neZha.ServoTypeList._360, neZha.ServoList.S2, 0)
        basic.pause(500)
    }
    basic.showIcon(IconNames.Yes)
    Running = false
})
stages.focusCode:
let Running = false
basic.showIcon(IconNames.Yes)
input.onLogoEvent(TouchButtonEvent.Touched, function () {
    Running = true
    basic.showIcon(IconNames.SmallDiamond)
    basic.showIcon(IconNames.Yes)
    Running = false
})
stages.focusNote: State/display excerpt. Insert the retained ten-wave loop between the diamond and the final tick. See Full program.

stages.title: Ignore touches while busy
stages.concept: A condition uses Running to prevent overlapping sequences.
stages.adds: Wrap the existing handler body in if not Running. Set true before waving and false after the final tick.
stages.predict: Will touching during a wave start more waves?
observe: Touch while busy: no extra cycle starts.
After the tick, touch to run ten again.
stages.question: Why must Running become false at the end?
stages.focusNote: Guard excerpt. Keep the diamond, ten-wave loop, and tick between the two assignments. See Full program for placement.
